A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VLA-Arena. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable matching of retained, relocated and newly added content.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulation results for six VLA models, perturbation experiments, data-composition ablations and comparisons with LIBERO.

after.justification: V2 retains original simulation experiments and adds newer-model evaluations, visual-grounding results, failure analyses and physical-robot experiments.

M1.justification: The core benchmark construction, difficulty levels, WordNet substitutions, visual perturbations and CBDDL procedures remain unchanged after matching v1 Sections 7–8 with v2 Appendices E–F. The added diagnostic experiments do not establish a revision to the proposed framework's algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: The original 170 simulation tasks and demonstration dataset are retained. V2 adds physical-robot counterparts across all four task dimensions, including real lighting and camera shifts, and a bounding-box localization task using UnseenObjects observations (Section 5 and Appendix H.5). These substantially extend environment and task coverage.

E2.justification: Alongside the original six models, v2 Tables 7–8 evaluate π0.5, GR00T-N1.6 and six Qwen2.5/3-VL variants using PI, OFT or GR00T architectures. Table 3 adds Qwen3-VL-8B as a grounding comparator, and Table 11 compares six models physically. The benchmark-feature comparison in Table 1 is separate from these evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: V1 specifies 20 evaluation episodes in Section 4.1 but 10 per task in Section 10.4; v2 consistently specifies 30 per task. Camera-selection documentation changes from discarding wrist views to retaining both wrist and third-person views. V2 also introduces physical trial protocols and localization evaluation using manually annotated boxes with IoU > 0.5. These are reported setting changes, without establishing exactly which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds VLM-versus-VLA grounding diagnostics, difficulty-specific ranking analysis, cross-layer attention comparisons, dynamic-failure categorization and physical visual-perturbation tests. Figure 2 removes the DynamicDistractors perturbation panels. The original data-diversity ablation is retained unchanged as Table 9, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: V1 mentions episode-level random seeds but provides no corresponding uncertainty estimates. V2 specifies three evaluation seeds with ten episodes each and adds systematic SR and CC variance reporting for the original six models in Table 31. This establishes a substantial reporting change, not additional independent training runs.

E6.justification: The main results change beyond rounding: OpenVLA's StatePreservation L2 SR is 0.34 in v1 Table 1 and 0.7 in v2 Table 2. These are revised reports under changed documented settings, not demonstrated same-setting gains. V2 also adds extensive newer-model, grounding, ranking and physical-robot results; Table 3 reports 93.3% Qwen3-VL-8B grounding accuracy at V4.

T1.justification: Appendix H.5.2 adds the formal grounding-success criterion I[IoU(Bpred, Bgt) > 0.5]. The explicit CC equation in v2 Section 2.1 restates the instantaneous-plus-terminal aggregation with α = 10 already documented in v1 Section 7.4.2. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: V2 recasts perturbations as diagnostic grounding probes and replaces asymmetric robustness as a principal finding with superficial visual perception, explicitly including catastrophic forgetting. Its abstract also adds the claim that rank reversals demonstrate complementary information across difficulty levels. The benchmark's task-count and framework contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: V2 adds causal explanations involving fine-tuning-induced forgetting, disruption of VLM priors by parallel decoding, and preservation through gradient isolation. It also hypothesizes why moving distractors are filtered out and interprets physical failures as validating simulation diagnostics. The introduction newly qualifies perturbations as diagnostic probes rather than faithful reproductions of real-world conditions.

D1.justification: V2 adds the grounding prompt, structured output format and annotation instructions, identifies the physical platform and task setups, and discloses simulator frequency and distractor displacement rates. It revises camera-selection instructions. Existing training hyperparameter tables, demonstration-processing procedures and framework access information are largely retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds a substantial benchmark-positioning matrix covering works such as AGNOSTOS, Gembench, COLOSSEUM, RL4VLA, INT-ACT and RoboCasa. It also adds references supporting newer models and visual-perturbation rationales. The introduction revises the research gap from overlooked extrapolation toward insufficient integration of robustness and extrapolation.

P1.justification: The main experimental narrative is substantially reorganized into failure modes, grounding diagnosis, disentangled rankings and ablation sections. CBDDL receives a separate preliminary subsection, while existing data-diversity and detailed performance discussions move to Appendix A. Extensive rewriting accompanies the diagnostic framing and the reorganized appendices.

P2.justification: The main results display changes from sparklines to a numerical grid with level-specific colors, shaded zeros and trend markers. Figure 2 is reduced from three task rows to two. V2 adds benchmark, grounding, ranking, physical-evaluation and variance tables plus physical-scene and attention visualizations, while relocating retained displays within a new document layout.

improvement.justification: V2 provides physical evidence for deployment-related failures that v1 supported only in simulation, broadens architecture comparisons and adds uncertainty reporting. These strengthen the evidential basis, but the net gain is limited by reporting and interpretation problems: Appendix A retains obsolete numerical examples, Table 2's zero CautiousGrasp L0 costs conflict with Table 31's nonzero variances, and the cross-model grounding comparison does not isolate fine-tuning-induced catastrophic forgetting.
